title: Bounded-above finite-free model at a cohomological upper bound
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $b$ be an integer and let $C$ be an object of the derived category $D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. If $C$ is pseudo-coherent [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex], equivalently it admits a quasi-isomorphism from a bounded-above complex of finitely generated projective $R$-modules, and $H^i(C)=0$ for every $i>b$, then there is a quasi-isomorphism $P^\bullet\to C$ from a complex $P^\bullet$ of finitely generated free $R$-modules with $P^i=0$ for every $i>b$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 15.66.5 (used in Lemma 15.76.2, Tag 0658)

proof.text: Unpack the definition IsPseudoCoherent to obtain a bounded-above finite free representative E with an isomorphism Q(E) ≅ C. For a fixed target bound b, induct on a natural number k, proving the conclusion for every such representative supported at most b+k. The zero case returns the representative itself. An arbitrary initial bound n is at most b+(n-b).toNat, including n<b.

In the successor case put n=b+k+1. The homologyFunctorFactors isomorphism and the image of Q(E) ≅ C under homologyFunctor identify H^n(E) with H^n(C), which is zero since n>b. Thus E is exact in degree n. Its outgoing differential is zero, because its target in degree n+1 is zero. ShortComplex.exact_iff_epi makes the incoming differential E^(n-1) → E^n epic. Freeness of E^n supplies its categorical projectivity, and Projective.factorThru applied to the identity supplies a section.

Apply the split-top cancellation theorem to this representative, its bound n, its finite free terms, and the section. Obtain a finite free L supported at most n-1 and a quasi-isomorphism π:L → E. Its image under Q is an isomorphism; compose with Q(E) ≅ C. Since n-1=b+k, apply the induction hypothesis to L.
